_description: People Alex can talk to. Each character (the key, e.g. "ruth", is used to place them on a map): 'name' (short name under their face in the chat), 'title' (heading of the conversation pop-up), 'look' (built-in outfit: 0 = farmer with straw hat and overalls, 1 = council member in a suit and tie), 'mood' ("sad", "angry" or "neutral": their face on the map and in the chat), 'button' (label of the closing button), 'lines' (the conversation in order; 'from' is "alex" or "them"), 'after' (blocks shown under the conversation, e.g. a note and citations; same block types as popups.json), 'countsTowardCompletion' (default true). To put someone on a map, add { "character": "ruth", "x": .., "y": .. } to that map's 'npcs': they stand there and a speech bubble appears over them. 'timing' sets how fast conversations play, in milliseconds: before each message a "typing" bubble shows for typingBase + typingPerLetter × the message length (at most typingMax), then 'pause' passes before the next message.
_usedIn: Simulation page → the valley (talking to people) and the conversation pop-ups

ruth._location: The park, beside the well (valley map)
ruth.name: Ruth
ruth.title: Ruth, a farmer

lines.text: Hi Ruth. Are you okay? You look worn out.
I’ve been carrying buckets all morning. My family has farmed this valley for three generations, and lately our well hasn't been giving us nearly enough water.
Do you think it’s because of the new data center?
I don't know. That's what worries me. Nobody ever told us how much water that place would need, or whether it would affect our wells.
I still can't believe they approved something this big without giving us a proper chance to speak.
Exactly. All we wanted was a chance to ask questions. What happens to our water? Our electricity bills? Our farms? Nobody seemed to have answers.
I've heard some neighbors are organizing to bring these concerns back to the council.
Good. Other communities have made their voices heard. We deserve that chance too.

johnson._location: Town plaza, by the town hall (valley map)
johnson.name: James Johnson
johnson.title: Councilmember Johnson

lines.text: Councilmember Johnson, why did the council agree to the data center?
They promised jobs and resources that would benefit our local economy. Most of those jobs ended up being short term with a focus on construction.
Did anyone know what we were agreeing to?
We signed a Community Benefits Agreement before we even knew of the impacts of the data center. Their lobbyists were in my office every week and pushing us to sign the document.
My water is brown and my bills keep going up.

I hear that every day now. So I'm co-sponsoring a new bill: the data center has to report its water and power use and pay for the damages it has caused. Next time, this town gets the facts before the signing.
